content.comment_body: I am seeking a way to configure an output so that it is active for seven short and one long period while the input remains active. This device will be installed on a boat and, because of the challenging environment, I decided not to use Arduino. Instead, I purchased a [company_name] starter pack. While I am comfortable with standard programming languages, I am new to PLC programming and would appreciate some advice. My main question is: Can you manually code a program on [product_name]? Or do you need to use graphical blocks to create it? I want to set up Output1 so it is controlled by Input1. While Input1 is active, Output1 should follow this cycle: { { Active (500 ms) Not active (500 ms) } repeated 7 times Active (3000 ms) Not active (1000 ms) } The whole sequence should repeat continuously as long as the input is active. Any suggestions or guidance would be greatly appreciated.
Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. Programming on this platform is possible only using LAD or FBD graphical block languages. I've attached a possible solution for you.

Dear [user_name], Thank you for your swift response and extremely helpful solution. Your guidance exceeded my expectations. After experimenting with the program you shared, I now understand how it works, though I doubt I would have been able to create it myself. It looks like I should review logic fundamentals if I plan to keep working with [product_name].
Hello [user_name], Thank you for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users trust the reliability of [company_name] products for challenging environments, such as boats, preferring them over platforms like Arduino. Newcomers with text-based coding experience find the graphical block-oriented programming (LAD or FBD) on [product_name] unfamiliar and seek help implementing custom timing sequences. The community is responsive and provides clear guidance, supporting beginner users and making it easier for them to get started.
